title: RAW bodily endpoint projection versus Fortune reversal over orar, oraiin and or or aiin
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_EXECUTED; partial mechanism, not a full reading. The complete Cgm 5185 Death argument motivates one common bodily endpoint for rich and poor. Three guessed values plus two derived forms impose convergence and nested absorption on actual f85r2 spans; written participants, output assertions and most groups remain unbound. IDEA000079 is not reopened by repetition alone.

design.author_role: Bounded independent producer; root owns review and selection; no access to 558/560 frozen drafts.
design.question: Can one written endpoint constructor, shared by two living-condition inputs and serial self-composition, constrain a whole f85r2 account of earthly transience more than five independent glosses would?
design.main_limit: There is presently no target-owned output assertion, common participant or time reference. This is a concrete incomplete meaning mechanism, not a tested operation or a complete source-to-target translation. If the old missing output remains, no executor should be built.

source.unit: Complete Death poem, 30 lines, Cgm 5185 17r-v; contextual controls are the complete Fortune and three-times/human-misery poems, each30 lines. These are formally separate units, not one sentence or one composite physician-to-cosmos proof.
source.native_status: Root source report contains a complete provisional native sense reading; this producer read that report and did not open images. Exact line uncertainties, double-leaf foliation and chronology limits remain.
source_implied_edges: Death catches a living human during pleasure; the cord is explicitly named in Death5-6.
Famous people have died; Death19-20 includes both poor and rich, young and old. The universal mortality claim does not distinguish those classes.
Death21-30 redirects the reader toward willing devout death, prayer and eternal life; bodily mortality is not destruction of the person or a denial of salvation.
Fortune9-10 gives rich today/in need tomorrow AND alive today/dead tomorrow. Human-misery17-18 repeats rich-to-poor. Fortune therefore cannot be excluded merely by the presence of mortality.

historical_limits: Catalogue witness date1486 is later than the target dating window; no copying direction, exemplar date or target provenance follows.
The source has several adjacent moral/cosmological poems, not a proved physician-to-time-to-cosmos argument.
The source never says Death is applied twice. The serial projection and its finite abstraction are new semantic assumptions, not a transcribed source assertion.
The source does not prove that wealth literally ceases to exist at death; only the selected bodily-end summary discards current wealth.
The theological conclusion preserves eternal life and personal identity. A terminal bodily summary is not an all-time world model and cannot be used to reject resurrection.

typed_semantics.operator_scope: Query the selected condition through its first earthly bodily-death endpoint and return only that endpoint summary. The third row is an algebraic re-projection, not a second physical killing. No spiritual fate, later resurrection, physical duration, wealth amount or named individual is encoded.
typed_semantics.term_grammar: ProfileTerm := ar | aiin | orar | oraiin | or ProfileTerm. Prefix free-token or consumes exactly one complete ProfileTerm. The two compounds are exact whole-form licenses with the same operation, not a general permission to segment other strings.

typed_semantics.person_application_requirement: A whole assertion must explicitly bind a written PersonTerm and a profile/endpoint/time relation, or explicitly quantify over persons using a written quantifier. These constructions are not supplied here. Re-projection retains the same profile input chain but does not by itself identify any person across lines.

conditional_target_consequences: Under this fixed typing, orar and oraiin denote the same coarse endpoint profile even though the inputs ar and aiin differ. Same profile does not identify the rich and poor persons.

N.2 or or aiin, N.4 oraiin and the exact separated or aiin spans must have one endpoint-profile value. A whole account requiring those expressions to denote different profiles would reject this fixed mechanism.

A whole account that uses N.2 as a return to living poverty selects the reversible Fortune rival instead. A written one-way change merely to poverty selects the impoverishment rival below rather than the mortality projection.
A purely bare sequence of these terms supplies none of those assertion outcomes by itself. The conditional predictions are model consequences, not already observed manuscript facts.

strongest_known_countercases: No existing target assertion independently reads the endpoint state. IDEA000079 therefore remains missing-design, not solved by the chosen source and repeated tokens.

The complete source does not express two applications of Death, and its Fortune poem also expressly contains death. The proposed absorption is a model restriction, not a unique historical identification.
For some literal free-or contexts even an argument of the required Profile type is missing; there are no hidden filler values.
The source body-versus-spirit distinction precludes treating terminality as permanent annihilation or an all-events physical simulator.
GDT1043 resolves neither Death nor Fortune as a target panel identity. South beads/staff support an elder/Autumn family as well; no skeleton/skull or source cord ownership is established there.
IT/RF W.20 and IT W.22 remove preferred separated applications without contradicting those editions; edition-specific completeness is required.
